patch.value: Worm and prameha names kept in Sanskrit with literal glosses only; no identifications. yūkā (louse) and pipīlikā (literally 'ant') are given their word meanings only; yūkā is kept as printed (f. nom. sg., collective; a plural yūkāḥ would keep its visarga before p). jantumātaraḥ is the nom. pl. of jantumātṛ (f.). Counting: worms 2 + 6 + 7 + 5 = 20, as stated; yonivyāpad 4 + 16 = 20, sixteen names given. Prameha count as printed: ten names summed as daśa śleṣmanimittāḥ, then eight names (kṣāra, kāla, nīla, lohita, mañjiṣṭhā, haridrā, hasti, madhu) summed as catvāro vātanimittāḥ: eighteen names in all against the twenty stated twice, and no Pitta group is named; the translation follows the print. ikṣubālikārasa kept as printed (bālikā; b/v spelling not flagged); bālikā cannot mean 'girl' here, ikṣubālikā is read as one plant name. śleṣmikī is kept as printed (vātikī and paittikī have vṛddhi, this form does not). doṣadūṣyasaṃsargaprakṛtinirdeśaiḥ: the analysis 'designations by the combination of doṣa and dūṣya, and by nature (prakṛti)' is medium; prakṛti could also mean the nature of the woman. The f. nom. pl. avaśiṣṭāḥ agrees with yonivyāpadaḥ (f.).
